verdict: Bengaluru retains classic late-cycle froth signals — inventory building faster than absorption (Q2 2026 unsold +34% YoY), launch mix heavily skewed to luxury (~96% of Q2 launches ≥₹80L), and wide asking-vs-guidance gaps in premium locales — but system-level shock absorbers (housing GNPA ~0.5%, EMI/income 35%, repo held at 5.25% on 5 Aug 2026) keep it out of distress. RBI's Aug MPC unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance; typical home-loan rates have drifted lower to ~7.75–8.15% (starting 7.25% at SBI) on the cumulative 125 bps easing. Composite tilt vs 2 Aug update: broadly unchanged — MPC decision known (hold), mortgage rate marginally lower.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.value: Bengaluru unsold +34% YoY in Q2 2026; pan-India unsold ~6.16 lakh units
indicators.note: Anarock Q2 2026: Bengaluru recorded the sharpest inventory build-up among the top 7 cities at +34% YoY, while sales rose only ~1% YoY on a weak base. Launches ~21,670 units (+41% YoY) sharply outpaced absorption. Pan-India unsold stock hit ~6.16 lakh units (+10% YoY) against ~90,715 units sold in the quarter — implying roughly 6–7 quarters to sell, worst in the post-pandemic cycle. Overhang concentrated in East Bengaluru (Whitefield, Sarjapur); Q3 2026 report due end-Sep.

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.note: Anarock Q2 2026 pan-India breakdown: ₹80L–1.5Cr = 27% of launches, ₹1.5–2.5Cr = 25%, above ₹2.5Cr = 22%. Only ~4% of new supply catered to sub-₹80L buyers — Bengaluru mirrors this skew. Developers continue to pivot to premium as mid-segment demand thins and inventory pressure builds. Unchanged since 2 Aug 2026 update.

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.note: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026: Bengaluru EMI/income worsened marginally to 35% (from 34% in H2 2025) despite ~125 bps of cumulative RBI easing. RBI Aug MPC (3–5 Aug 2026) unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance; next MPC 5–7 Oct 2026. Typical home-loan rates now ~7.75–8.15% (SBI starts at 7.25%, HDFC at 7.75%). H2 2026 Knight Frank release expected Dec 2026.
indicators.src: Knight Frank Affordability Index H1 2026; RBI MPC Aug 2026

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: RBI Financial Stability Report June 2026: housing-loan GNPA at 0.5%; system GNPA at multi-decade low of 1.8%, projected to rise only to 1.9% by Mar 2028 under baseline. Secured retail GNPA 0.7%; unsecured retail 1.7% flagged for watch as non-housing retail now 58.4% of household borrowing. CRAR 17.7%, CET1 15.3%. Next FSR due Dec 2026.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.note: Indiranagar guidance ~₹12k/sqft vs market asking ₹18–22k/sqft (50–83% premium). Newer corridors (Devanahalli, Hoskote) narrower at 15–25% and partially compressed after the Feb 2026 BBMP guidance hike (6–15%). A further statewide 12–30% zone-wise revision was announced in May 2026 but is still not gazette-notified as of Aug 2026 — sub-registrars remain split on which value to apply. Wide gap in prime pockets remains a clear froth signal.

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.value: Karnataka FY25–26 stamps revenue ~₹20,837 cr (record); Jul 2026 monthly not yet published
indicators.note: Karnataka Stamps & Registration posted a record ~₹20,837 cr in FY25–26 (largely Bengaluru). Headline revenue is inflated by the Aug 2025 fee doubling (1%→2%) and Feb 2026 guidance hike — transactional volume growth is softer than revenue growth. Kaveri 2.0 fully live statewide (biometric-only in-person step); IGR Karnataka has not yet published Jul 2026 monthly aggregates. Kaveri 3.0 (AI-driven) rollout flagged for FY26–27.
